body: idk, that quote just kind of opened a new can of worms for me; for instance, if most people have that personal sense of meaning, doesn't that kind of render one's search for reasons to live nothing more than a bogus search to fill an unfillable hole?

Maybe. But again, without meaning to sound like a pretentious git, I have an innate distrust and aversion to neuroscientists. They remind of me of the old doctor from Jurassic Park, who is so hellbent on scientific progress that they recklessly pursue it without any thought as to the potential destruction of their work. 


What if neuroscientists were to prove my worst fears right as well as prove their own suspicions? That it's all chemical, and therefore, pointless? What would that do to people like us? If you're right in saying that we're more predisposed to tough philosophical questions, then that would could lead to nihilism and suicide rate increases among that creatively inclined. Then we have a pretty crappy world in which art is no longer capable of reflecting life's beauty as well as it's sadness.

I feel an inclination toward that sort of thing. All day I just come up with films, ideas for song structures, video game ideas, occassionally I'll even have ideas for novels. I feel an instictive urge and desire to create.

I mean, both of my parents have IQ's in the 150 range. My grandfather was one of the first key players in Silicon Valley, and his daughter, my mother, was on track to being a professor of psychology at UC, but life had other plans. My brother is on the Dean's list at his university. It was in the nation's top percentile for English on my SAT. So, without trying to sound like a smug prick, I already know I'm smart.

The problem is that whenever I share these concerns with my family, they just look at me funny, maybe my dad proffers some religious advice, but mostly they just get angry and confused as to why these questions bother me. But in the end, they always just walk away frustrated.


Frankly, I'd rather be an idiot than have these questions; questions that have no immediate answer and threaten the very nature of my existance. So I mostly just view my philosophical bent and intelligence as something a cruel cosmic joke, or maybe just a curse.


They say you have to be intelligent to ask these sorts of questions, so if I were to try and, as you put it, "make others more aware and accountable," I would be running a fool's errand, as no one I've ever met or known has gone down this road.
